    ENDIF

ENDFUNCTION

items.stem: Harbour Bank in Santiago needs a program that repeatedly inputs the weight of a parcel in kg. Input stops when a weight of 0 is entered. Parcels over 12 kg cost $12, parcels over 2 kg up to 12 kg cost $7 and other parcels cost $4. (a) Write pseudocode that outputs the cost of each parcel and the total cost at the end. (b) Justify your choice of loop.
items.answer:
Total ← 0
INPUT Weight
WHILE Weight <> 0
    IF Weight > 12 THEN
        Cost ← 12
    ELSE
        IF Weight > 2 THEN
            Cost ← 7
        ELSE
            Cost ← 4
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT Cost
    Total ← Total + Cost
    INPUT Weight
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT Total
(b) A pre-condition loop, because the number of parcels is not known and the first input may be 0.
items.markingKey: (a) initialise total [1]; input before loop and inside loop [1]; loop ends on 0 [1]; correct selection for three bands [2]; output cost and add to total [1]; output total after loop [1] (b) [1]

items.stem: Ravi records podcasts for FreshFarm Foods and needs to upload them quickly. (a) Describe how analogue sound is converted into a digital sound file. (b) Explain the effect of halving the sampling rate on the file and on the quality. (c) Recommend, with a reason, whether lossy or lossless compression should be used for the archive. (d) Give one reason why sampled sound can never be an exact copy of the original analogue sound.
items.answer: (a) The amplitude of the sound wave is measured (sampled) at regular intervals and each sample is stored as a binary number using an ADC. (b) File size halves; fewer samples so the recording is less accurate and high frequencies are lost. (c) Lossless, so that the original recording is preserved exactly for future use (or lossy if storage is very limited, accepting some loss). (d) The amplitude between samples is not recorded and each sample is rounded to the nearest level.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: sampled at regular intervals; 1 mark: amplitude stored as binary; 1 mark: ADC [3] (b) 1 mark: file size halves; 1 mark: lower quality / less accurate [2] (c) 1 mark: choice; 1 mark: justification [2] (d) 1 mark [1]

items.stem: MetroBus in Cape Town needs a program that repeatedly inputs the weight of a parcel in kg. Input stops when a weight of 0 is entered. Parcels over 6 kg cost $12, parcels over 2 kg up to 6 kg cost $7 and other parcels cost $4. (a) Write pseudocode that outputs the cost of each parcel and the total cost at the end. (b) Justify your choice of loop.
items.answer:
Total ← 0
INPUT Weight
WHILE Weight <> 0
    IF Weight > 6 THEN
        Cost ← 12
    ELSE
        IF Weight > 2 THEN
            Cost ← 7
        ELSE
            Cost ← 4
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    OUTPUT Cost
    Total ← Total + Cost
    INPUT Weight
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT Total
(b) A pre-condition loop, because the number of parcels is not known and the first input may be 0.
items.markingKey: (a) initialise total [1]; input before loop and inside loop [1]; loop ends on 0 [1]; correct selection for three bands [2]; output cost and add to total [1]; output total after loop [1] (b) [1]

items.stem: An array Scores holds 50 integers. (a) Write pseudocode for a bubble sort that sorts Scores into ascending order and stops early if no swaps are made in a pass. (b) Explain why the number of comparisons in each pass can be reduced by one each time.
items.answer:
Boundary ← 49
REPEAT
    NoSwaps ← TRUE
    FOR j ← 1 TO Boundary
        IF Scores[j] > Scores[j + 1] THEN
            Temp ← Scores[j]
            Scores[j] ← Scores[j + 1]
            Scores[j + 1] ← Temp
            NoSwaps ← FALSE
        ENDIF
    NEXT j
    Boundary ← Boundary - 1
UNTIL NoSwaps = TRUE OR Boundary = 0
(b) After each pass the largest remaining value is in its final place at the end, so it need not be compared again.
items.markingKey: (a) outer loop until no swaps [1]; flag reset/set [1]; inner loop with correct bound [1]; comparison of adjacent elements [1]; swap using temp [1]; boundary reduced [1] (b) [1]

items.stem: Noah needs a subroutine IsEven for Lakeside College that returns TRUE if an integer is even and FALSE otherwise. Write the pseudocode for IsEven.
items.answer:
FUNCTION IsEven(N : INTEGER) RETURNS BOOLEAN
    IF N MOD 2 = 0 THEN
        RETURN TRUE
    ELSE
        RETURN FALSE
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

items.stem: Coral Bay Aquarium in Colombo runs many programs at the same time on each computer. Discuss, with reasons, the importance of interrupts in a multitasking operating system.
items.answer: Points in favour: devices signal when ready so CPU does not waste time polling; urgent events handled at once; enables time-slicing via timer interrupts. Points against / limitations: too many interrupts add overhead from saving/restoring registers; badly prioritised interrupts can delay important tasks. Conclusion: interrupts are essential for efficient multitasking but need careful priority management.
